predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Trebizond and 'the surrounding province of Chaldia', the Byzantine theme seized by Alexios and David Komnenos in April 1204, weeks before the sack of Constantinople

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: the whole remaining empire, surrendered by David on 15 August 1461

successors.name: Principality of Theodoro
successors.text: Crimean Gothia (Mangup/Theodoro), the inland part of Perateia, where the Gabras family 'established the Principality of Theodoro'

successors.name: Republic of Genoa
successors.text: the Crimean coast towns (Caffa, Soldaia 1365, Cembalo) that became Genoese Gazaria

rulers.name: Irene Palaiologina, Anna Anachoutlou, John III, Michael

ledger.x: 'Alexios took possession of Limnia, Samsun and Sinope.'
1204: Theodore I Laskaris page, the paragraph on Sept-Dec 1204: 'David Komnenos launched a military campaign into Paphlagonia and occupied the towns along the Black Sea coast' (no town named there).
Perateia (Cherson, Kerch and hinterlands) 'made... a tributary to Trebizond'; 'Trapezuntine control over Perateia had been weak almost from the beginning'.

'In April 1204, while Constantinople was occupied with the on-going conflict with the Fourth Crusade, David and Alexios occupied the city of Trebizond'; 'Immediately that city, Oinaion and Sinope declared for the two brothers.'
Unsuccessful Seljuk siege of Trebizond 'around the year 1205'.
Trebizond and its approaches.
1208: David Komnenos page, 'In 1208 Laskaris renewed his offensive against David Komnenos' and 'invested Heraclea Pontica'; Henry of Flanders then occupied Nicomedia and Laskaris lifted the siege.
Battle of Antioch on the Meander page: 'in 1212, the death of David Komnenos allowed their annexation of his lands in Paphlagonia'.
Empire of Trebizond page: 'the territories west of Sinope were lost to Theodore I Laskaris by 1214'.

Empire of Trebizond page: 'the territories west of Sinope were lost to Theodore I Laskaris by 1214'; moved from 1212 on 2026-10-19 to agree with nicaean-empire /ledger/15 (1214), the year the last Paphlagonian land west of Sinope went.
Siege of Sinope page: the city 'surrendered on 1 November' and, 'apart from a period of Trapezuntine recovery in 1254-1265, the city henceforth remained in Turkish hands'.

Alexios I of Trebizond page: 'The loss of Sinope pushed the western frontier of Komnenine territories, which had been at Heraclea a few years earlier, back to the Iris and Thermodon rivers, only 250 kilometres (160 mi) from their base at Trebizond'; the same page has Alexios taking 'Limnia, Samsun and Sinope' in 1204.
Seljuk siege of Trebizond 1222-1223, broken by a storm during the night assault.
Trebizond and its approaches.
'In 1223 the Seljuk governor of Sinope sent ships to attack the coast of Trapezuntine Crimea'; Andronikos sent a fleet against Sinope.
the Perateia coast.
Oinaion Trapezuntine 1228-1230.
Oinaion (Unye) and its fortress.
A Fallmerayer-era claim repeated on the Andronikos I page; the extent of any Trapezuntine Lazica is unknown and the Cliopatria shapes never reach beyond Batumi.
Oinaion Trapezuntine 1243-1297.
'On 24 June 1254, Manuel recaptured Sinope, and made Ghadras archon of the Black Sea port', under an Ilkhanid yarligh.
'Permanent loss of Sinope: 1265' (to the Pervane Mu'in al-Din Suleiman, nominally Seljuk).
'Though King David failed to take the city, the Georgians occupied several provinces.'
Treaty of 1282 with Michael VIII: John II gave up 'Emperor and Autocrat of the Romans' for 'Emperor and Autocrat of all the East, the Iberians, and the Transmarine Provinces'.
End of the Georgian occupation is not dated; assumed within a year.
Panaretos: 'during his reign the Turks seized Chalybia and launched a great invasion, so that all those places became uninhabited' (John II, 1280-1297); year a midpoint.
Haciemiroglu 1297-1302.
Oinaion Trapezuntine 1302-1346; Alexios II 'defeated a Turkoman invasion' that had sacked Kerasous in 1301 or 1302 and fortified the town.
Genoese demands refused 1306; fighting in which 'the Genoese set fire to the suburbs of Trebizond'; peace treaties 1314 and 1316.
the Genoese quarter and suburbs of Trebizond.
Cliopatria's convention: Crimea leaves the Trebizond row and the Theodoro row begins in 1333.
'Emirate of Haciemiroglu between 1297-1302 and 1346-1461'; main page 1347-48 'conquering Oinaion and besieging Trebizond'.
'the Genoese seized Kerasus' (1347-1348).

Genoese hold of Kerasous ended with 'the concession of Leonkastron to the Genoese in 1349' (a fort at Trebizond); by 1354 Kerasous was the base of the rebel megas doux Niketas, retaken by Alexios III in May 1355.
Sub-cell; recorded for completeness.
Alexios III page: 'By June 1354 the megas doux was forced to flee to Kerasous', where he prepared a fleet; the rebels sailed against Trebizond in March 1355 but 'abandoned their expedition'.
ledger.cp: Niketas Scholares and the Scholarioi rebels

ledger.x: Alexios III 'suffered a major defeat in battle in 1355' while 'strengthening the frontier against the Turkmen'; no town named; Aq Qoyunlu stands for the Turkmen of Bayburt.

Alexios III page: 'In May 1355' the emperor 'conquered the town in the absence of Niketas'; his cavalry then besieged 'the last fortress loyal to the megas doux, Kenchrina' (location not given, so not drawn) and obtained its surrender; Niketas 'died in 1360' in Trebizond.
ledger.cp: Niketas Scholares and the Scholarioi rebels

ledger.x: 'Between the two dates [1384 and 1386], Limnia irrevocably slipped from Trapezuntine control and became a Turkoman possession' (Tajeddin, emir of Limnia, husband of Alexios III's daughter Eudokia since 8 October 1379).
Siege 14 September 1460 - 15 August 1461; 'On 15 August 1461, Sultan Mehmed II entered Trebizond'; Mesochaldia submitted to Hizir; Bryer: pockets resisted up to ten years.
the whole empire.

wars.name: Nicaean-Trapezuntine war in Paphlagonia
wars.outcome: Nicaea took Heraclea and Amastris (1212) and the rest of Paphlagonia west of Sinope (1214); Rum took Sinope (1 November 1214)

wars.name: Siege of Sinope (1214)
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory 1 November 1214; Alexios I captured; tributary status

wars.name: Seljuk siege of Trebizond (1222-1223)
wars.outcome: Trapezuntine victory; vassalage to Iconium ended

wars.name: Georgian siege of Trebizond (1282)
wars.outcome: City held; Georgians occupied several provinces temporarily

wars.name: Turkmen invasion and sack of Kerasous (1301/02)
wars.outcome: Trapezuntine victory; Turkmen general captured; Kerasous fortified

wars.name: Trapezuntine civil wars
wars.outcome: Alexios III secured the throne (22 December 1349); the megas doux Niketas Scholares rebelled from Kerasous in 1354 and was crushed in May 1355; Oinaion to the Turks, Leonkastron to Genoa

certainty.note: A coastal strip whose inland edge is the Pontic watershed; the western frontier (Thermodon, Oinaion, Limnia) moved with Turkmen pressure and is dated by single mentions.
